literal: Fear to those who possess, fortress is not; like that is not, negligence to those who possess, good.
translation: Just as a fortress is of no use to those gripped by fear, there is no good for those who are negligent.
modern: அச்சம் உடையவர்களுக்கு அரண் இருந்தாலும் பயனில்லை. அதுபோலவே, கடமையை மறக்கும் சோர்வு உடையவர்களுக்கு எந்த நன்மையும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet draws a direct comparison between fear and negligence. A strong fortress cannot protect soldiers who are paralyzed by fear, because their internal weakness renders the external defense useless. In the exact same way, no amount of external advantage can bring success to those who are negligent. The word poccappu means a lapse in attention or forgetfulness, an internal flaw that undermines all other strengths.
